surprises.description: The Cheesecake Factory comps came in far above the preview’s roughly 5%–6% expectation, with traffic growth of 9.5% rather than the expected 2%–3%. Positive 3.3% mix also helped drive the result, even though pricing was 2.4%, below the preview’s just-under-3% assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Cheesecake Factory restaurants delivered comparable sales growth of 15.2% in Q3 2026, with traffic growth of 9.5%”; comps were driven by “2.4% pricing, positive 3.3% mix … and 9.5% traffic.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “CAKE-brand comps +5.5%”; it said the base scenario was “+5% to +6%, traffic +2–3%.”

surprises.description: Revenue exceeded the preview’s roughly $1.00 billion base estimate and the street consensus range by a substantial amount, and was meaningfully above the company’s prior guidance ceiling. The preview expected a beat, but not revenue above $1.033 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues exceeded $1.033 billion, meaningfully above the high end of guidance, marking the second consecutive quarter of record revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave consensus revenue of “$994.6M–$998.5M” and a base estimate of “$1,000M”; prior company guidance was “$980–990M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS and net income margin both exceeded the preview’s effective earnings bar: EPS was slightly above the roughly $1.00 whisper, while the 5.1% margin was notably above the roughly 4.5% estimate. Adjusted EBITDA growth also showed stronger profitability than the preview’s seasonal-deleveraging concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.02 (GAAP $1.19), with adjusted net income margin of 5.1% and adjusted EBITDA up 38% year-over-year to $98.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the effective buy-side bar was “~$1.00 adj. EPS” and estimated “Adj. net income margin ~4.5% (derived).” It also said Q3 was seasonally lower-volume and expected sequential deleverage.

surprises.description: North Italia’s comps matched the preview’s expected range, but its mature restaurant-level margin fell sharply from 15.7% to 13.2%, a deterioration not anticipated in the preview. Management responded with a menu and happy-hour refresh and pilot media investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North Italia was a laggard with comparable sales down 3% and mature restaurant-level margin falling to 13.2% from 15.7%, prompting a new menu, happy hour refresh, and pilot media investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “North Italia still ~-1% to -3%” in the base case and noted Q2 comps of “-3%”; it did not forecast a margin decline.

surprises.description: The Q4 outlook includes flat traffic in the final three holiday weeks, rather than the positive traffic investors were hoping to hear about alongside the 4% pricing step-up. The revenue and margin guidance is strong, but the traffic assumption is a cautionary signal relative to the preview’s preferred scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 guidance assumes Q3 trends hold but “model[s] flat traffic in the final three holiday weeks minus a 1% holiday-shift headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said buy-side investors wanted Q4 comps of “+4% or better with traffic still positive” and warned that “any hedge on 4Q traffic at 4% pricing” would be read negatively.
